what: QXO is a roofing and building products distributor assembled by Brad Jacobs from 2024 onward, mainly by buying Beacon Roofing Supply. It delivers roofing, siding and waterproofing materials to contractors.
customers: Roofing and building contractors across North America, who need materials delivered to the job site.
money: membranes and insulation for flat roofs
moat: Branch density and delivery fleets, in a distribution business where the supplier who can get materials onto a roof the same day wins the order.
risks: A $676M net loss and negative free cash flow while the acquisitions are absorbed
$3.7B of debt taken on to buy Beacon
The whole thesis rests on management executing a roll-up that has barely begun
opportunities: Revenue went from $57M to $6.8B in a year and is $12.1B over the last twelve months
$2.4B of cash still available for further acquisitions
Analysts see about 109% upside, the widest gap on the list, with 18 covering the stock
watch: Organic branch sales growth and the margin as integration costs fall away.
